claim: The Olympic Museum is open Tuesday to Sunday 09:00–18:00, closed Mondays plus 24/25/31 December and 1 January, with last admission at 17:00.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday from 09:00 to 18:00 (9 AM to 6 PM), and closed on Mondays. The museum is closed on December 24, 25, 31 and January 1. Last admission at the museum is 5 p.m.

claim: Olympic Museum admission is CHF 20 full, CHF 14 reduced (seniors/students/disabled), free for children up to 15 with an accompanying adult.
quote: Full price (ages 16+): 20 CHF — Seniors, students, disabled visitors: 14 CHF — Children (up to 15 years): Free with accompanying adult

claim: Plateforme 10's three museums (MCBA, mudac, Photo Elysée) open 10:00–18:00; a combined 3-museum ticket is CHF 25 full / CHF 19 reduced, or CHF 15 for a single museum.
quote: Open from 10:00 to 18:00 ... Full price CHF 25.–, reduced price CHF 19.– ... I only want to visit this museum CHF 15.–

claim: Plateforme 10 is a 25,000 m² arts district by Lausanne station uniting MCBA (fine arts), Photo Elysée (photography) and mudac (contemporary design).
quote: Plateforme 10 is a 25,000 m² arts district in the heart of Lausanne, formed by the merger of the Musée Cantonal des Beaux-Arts (MCBA), Photo Elysée, and mudac

claim: Collection de l'Art Brut is open Tuesday–Sunday 11:00–18:00; admission is CHF 12 adult / CHF 6 reduced, free for under-18s and free for everyone on the first Saturday of each month.
quote: From Tuesday to Sunday: 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. ... Adult: CHF 12.– ... Reduced rate (AVS/AI, Caritas Culture Card, groups of 6 or more): CHF 6.– ... Free admission for everyone on the first Saturday of each month

claim: The Collection de l'Art Brut, founded around Jean Dubuffet's donation, marks its 50th anniversary in February 2026 and is housed in the 18th-century Château de Beaulieu.
quote: The Collection de l'Art Brut is marking its 50th anniversary in February 2026.

claim: Lausanne Cathedral is open daily 09:00–19:00 (Apr–Sep) or 09:00–17:30 (Oct–Mar); entry to the cathedral is free, climbing the belfry tower costs CHF 6 adult / CHF 4 reduced, free for under-25s, with last tower visit 30 minutes before closing.
quote: April 1 – September 30, 2026: Monday–Sunday: 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM ... Adults (26+): 6 CHF — Children & youth (up to 25): Free ... Last tower visit: 30 minutes before closing

claim: Lausanne's Cathedral, considered the finest Gothic edifice in Switzerland, retains the nightly tradition of a watchman (le guet) calling the hours from the belfry from 22:00 to 02:00.
quote: Since 1405, a tower watchman (le guet) called the hours and this tradition continues nightly from 22:00 to 2:00.

claim: Sauvabelin Tower is a 35-metre wooden tower above Lausanne with 302 steps and 360° panoramic views over the city, Lake Geneva, the Alps and the Jura; the surrounding park has a lake, oak forests and a small animal park.
quote: The Tower of Sauvabelin requires climbing 302 steps to reach its platform ... 35 metre high ... An artificial lake...surrounded by oak forests ... Goats, woolly pigs, ducks, wild boar and various birds

claim: Sauvabelin Tower has a double-helix staircase so visitors ascend and descend on opposite sides; access is capped at 30 people for safety and the tower closes in strong wind, snow or ice.
quote: a double helix structure, with visitors ascending and descending at opposite sides ... A maximum of 30 people at same time, for security reasons.

claim: Climbing Sauvabelin Tower is free of charge, making it a no-cost panoramic viewpoint in Lausanne.
quote: Entrance is free but limited to a maximum of 50 people at a time for security reasons.

claim: SS La Suisse is a 1910 Belle Époque paddle steamer, 78.5m long, 850-passenger capacity, fully restored in 2009 and based on the Upper Lake route from Lausanne.
quote: La Suisse... commissioned in 1910... the most beautiful steam boat in the world... capacity 850 passengers, length 78.5 meters... underwent a complete renovation in 2009.

claim: From Lausanne, SS La Suisse sails three times daily to St-Gingolph returning via the Lavaux vineyards, a roughly three-hour circular cruise, with stops at Vevey, Montreux and Château de Chillon.
quote: La Suisse cruises three times per day from Lausanne to St Gingolph and on to Chateau de Chillon before returning to Lausanne via the Lavaux, with three hours for the full circular cruise.

claim: CGN paddle-steamer cruises cost the same as the modern boats; a 2-hour Geneva afternoon cruise is CHF 33 (CHF 46 first class) and a Geneva–Lausanne return day ticket is CHF 64 (CHF 90 first class); Swiss rail passes and Half Fare Card are accepted.
quote: A 2-hour lunchtime or afternoon cruise on a paddle steamer from Geneva costs CHF33 (CHF46 First Class)... a day ticket costs CHF64 (CHF90 in first class)... Most Swiss railway and transportation discount passes and travel cards are accepted on CGN Lac Léman boats.

claim: Ouchy's tree-lined quays — first opened in 1901 — run from the Haldimand tower past Château d'Ouchy and continue east toward Lutry and west to Saint-Sulpice, with three gardens (Denantou, Elysée, Olympic Park) and a rose garden of 130+ species at Place du Général Guisan.
quote: richly flowered and tree-lined quays, first opened in 1901... promenade extends eastward toward Lutry and westward to Saint-Sulpice... Rose garden at Place du Général Guisan featuring more than 130 different species of rose.

claim: Ouchy is reached by the city's vertical M2 metro and offers pedalo rentals, biking, water-skiing lessons and views across to the Savoy Alps.
quote: Ouchy is a lakefront district in Lausanne, Switzerland, accessible via the city's vertical m2 metro from the train station... Pedalo rentals, Biking, Water skiing lessons... The Savoy-Alps summits are visible across the lake.

claim: Bellerive-Plage opens May 18 to Sept 1 (09:30–20:00) and Sept 2–16 (09:30–19:30), with an Olympic pool, a 10m diving board, three pools and a 350m supervised lake beach, plus volleyball, basketball and food kiosks.
quote: May 18 – September 1: 9:30 AM – 8:00 PM daily; September 2 – 16: 9:30 AM – 7:30 PM daily... three large pools, one with a ten-metre diving board... supervised lake beach spanning 350 meters.

claim: Plage de Vidy is the largest beach on Lake Geneva with over 500m of sand across multiple coves, set in Parc Louis Bourget with showers, playgrounds, volleyball, and rentals for stand-up paddleboards and pedal boats; entry is free.
quote: Vidy Beach is the largest beach and green space on Lake Geneva with over 500 metres of sand across multiple small coves... Water sports rentals (standup paddleboards, pedal boats)... Parc Louis Bourget, 1006 Lausanne.

claim: Bateaux-Location-Ouchy rents 4- and 5-seater pedal boats (with optional slide) next to the Ouchy port at CHF 15/30 min, CHF 25/hour, CHF 45/2 hours; life jackets and parasols are free, unaccompanied children must be 14+.
quote: 30 minutes: CHF 15; 60 minutes: CHF 25; 90 minutes: CHF 38; 2 hours: CHF 45... Life jackets and parasols provided free of charge... Unaccompanied children must be at least 14 years old.

claim: The M2 between Ouchy and Flon is a fully automated rubber-tyred line that opened in 2008 with a maximum 11.6% gradient — among the world's steepest metro lines — using MP89CA trains akin to Paris Métro Line 14.
quote: maximum gradient of 11.6% (1 in 8.66) on the Ouchy-Flon section... opened in 2008... fully automated... 15 two-car MP89CA trains, similar to those on Line 14 of the Paris Métro.

claim: The Lausanne M2 line is 5.9 km long across 14 stations, full run about 20 minutes, linking Ouchy on the lake to Lausanne railway station and the Flon hub where M1 and the LEB regional rail interchange.
quote: The Lausanne Métro Line M2 is 5.9 kilometres (3.7 mi) long... links the lakeside at Ouchy with Lausanne railway station and the core of the city at Flon. At Lausanne-Flon, passengers can transfer to M1 and the R20 service of leb... 14 stations, and the full running time is about 20 minutes.

claim: The classic Lavaux Route 113 from St-Saphorin to Lutry is 11.6 km, takes about 4 hours, with 200 m of ascent and 500 m of descent.
quote: Distance: 11.6 km ... Duration: Approximately 4 hours ... Elevation Gain: 200m up, 500m down ... The trail follows 'Route 113 – Terrasses de Lavaux' through wine terraces along Lake Geneva's north shore.

claim: AllTrails lists the St-Saphorin to Lutry vineyard terraces hike at about 7 miles (~11 km), 3.5-4 hours.
quote: The Lavaux Vineyard Terraces trail from St-Saphorin to Lutry covers 7 miles (approximately 11 km) and takes about 3.5–4 hours to complete.

claim: The full long-distance 'Discovering the Terraces of Lavaux' trail is about 35 km and ~8h30; Rivaz, St-Saphorin and Chexbres each have their own rail stations.
quote: The full 'Discovering the Terraces of Lavaux' long-distance trail (GT) spans '35 km' and 'should take around 8h30' ... All three towns (Rivaz, St Saphorin, Chexbres) 'have railway stations'

claim: Lavaux Vinorama in Rivaz showcases roughly 300 wines (notably Chasselas and indigenous Plant Robert) from across the eight Lavaux appellations.
quote: about 300 wines from across all the Lavaux vineyards including many Chasselas, the region's iconic grape variety, as well as elegant and powerful reds, white specialities and sweet wines

claim: Vinorama screens an 8-language documentary following a year in the life of a Lavaux winegrowing family and is open Mon-Sat 10:30-20:00, Sun until 19:00.
quote: An ultra-modern screening room features a documentary available in eight languages that follows 'the year of a Lavaux vine-growing family' ... Hours: Monday–Saturday 10:30–20:00; Sunday 10:30–19:00

claim: The Lavaux Express tourist train runs two main 1h15 loops at CHF 17 from April 1 to November 1 2026: Lutry-Aran-Grandvaux-Lutry and Cully-Riex-Epesses-Dezaley-Cully.
quote: Lutry Loop (CHF 17.-) ... Villages visited: 'Lutry - Aran - Grandvaux - Lutry' - Duration: 1 hour 15 minutes ... Cully Loop (CHF 17.-) ... 'Cully - Riex - Epesses - Dézaley - Cully' - Duration: 1 hour 15 minutes ... Operating: April 1 – November 1, 2026

claim: CGN boats from Lausanne-Ouchy reach Lutry in ~18 min, Cully in ~33 min and Rivaz-St-Saphorin in ~47 min, with 2-5 daily round trips mid-April to late October.
quote: Lausanne-Ouchy: 0:00 (departure) - Lutry: 0:18 - Cully: 0:33 - Rivaz-St Saphorin: 0:47 ... Peak Season (mid-April to late October): 'two round-trip cruises...are possible daily from Lausanne and a further three from Vevey'

claim: SBB regional trains link Lausanne to Cully in roughly 8-10 minutes, running about every 15 minutes, with stops in Pully, Lutry, Villette, Cully, Epesses, Rivaz and St-Saphorin.
quote: The fastest way to get from Lausanne to Cully is by train which takes 10 minutes ... Swiss Federal Railways (SBB CFF FFS) operates a train from Lausanne to Cully every 15 minutes ... The R4 ... stops at Pully, Lutry, Villette, Cully, Epesses, Rivaz, and St Saphorin between Lausanne and Vevey

claim: Saint-Saphorin is a celebrated Lavaux appellation between Epesses and Chardonne whose vineyards are planted overwhelmingly with Chasselas.
quote: Saint-Saphorin village lies on the steep northern shores of Lake Geneva, in Lavaux, Switzerland. Located immediately west of Chardonne and east of Puidoux and Epesses ... A typical vineyard in Saint-Saphorin is planted mostly with Fendant, or Chasselas

claim: Cully's 16th-19th-century winegrowers' houses make it a natural base for Lavaux, while Epesses is a tiny hamlet perched above the lake.
quote: Cully is an excellent starting point for exploring the vineyard terraces, with its historic center featuring narrow streets and picturesque winegrowers' houses dating from the 16th to 19th century. Tiny Epesses is nestled on a hillside above Lake Geneva

claim: Chillon Castle is officially the most visited historical monument in Switzerland, open daily April–September 9:00–19:00 with adult admission CHF 15; S5 regional trains run hourly from Lausanne to Veytaux-Chillon, a 6-minute walk away.
quote: S5 regional trains depart hourly to Veytaux-Chillon station, a 6-minute walk away. ... The site is recognized as 'the most visited historical monument in Switzerland.'

claim: From Lausanne to Veytaux-Chillon by train takes around 35 minutes with departures every 10–20 minutes; via Montreux it is 20 minutes to Montreux then 4 minutes onward.
quote: The train from Lausanne to Château de Chillon (Veytaux-Chillon) takes 35 minutes, with trains leaving roughly every 10 to 20 minutes.

claim: Montreux's lakeside Place du Marché hosts the bronze Freddie Mercury statue (unveiled 1996, by Czech sculptor Irena Sedlecká) in his Wembley-1986 pose, freely accessible on the flat Riviera promenade.
quote: The bronze statue of Czech sculptor Irena Sedlecká was unveiled in 1996 and stands on the Place du Marché directly on the lakeside promenade.

claim: Vevey is 20 minutes by train from Lausanne and combines Chaplin's World, the Alimentarium food museum, the giant lake-set Fork sculpture, and a walkable lakeside in one compact destination.
quote: Vevey sits on the main rail line between Lausanne (20 minutes) and Montreux (8 minutes), with frequent trains throughout the day.

claim: The Fork in front of the Alimentarium in Vevey is an 8-metre stainless-steel sculpture by Jean-Pierre Zaugg, installed 1995 for the museum's 10th anniversary and entered in the Guinness World Records in 2014 as the world's tallest fork.
quote: The Fork is made of stainless steel, 8 metres high and 1.3 metres wide. ... It has held the record in the Guinness World Records since 2014 as the world's tallest fork.

claim: Chaplin's World occupies the Manoir de Ban above Vevey in Corsier-sur-Vevey, where Charlie Chaplin spent the last 25 years of his life; the museum pairs his family home with a studio area for interactive film exhibits.
quote: Chaplin lived the final 25 years of his life in the large house Manoir de Ban in Corsier-sur-Vevey on the slopes overlooking Lake Geneva and the Alps.

claim: Gruyères day-trip from Lausanne takes about 1h15–1h30 by train with one or two transfers and centres on the 13th-century castle, La Maison du Gruyère cheese factory, HR Giger Museum, and a cobblestoned medieval town.
quote: The journey takes approximately 45 minutes by car or 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes by train with one or two transfers.

claim: There is no direct train from Lausanne to Gruyères; the fastest route runs via Palézieux in about 1h 45m with typical changes at Palézieux/Bulle.
quote: There is no direct train from Lausanne to Gruyères. You can take a train from Lausanne to Gruyères via Palézieux in around 1h 45m.

claim: The HR Giger Museum sits in St-Germain Castle in medieval Gruyères and houses the largest collection of the Alien designer's paintings, sculptures, furniture, and film sets; summer hours run 10:00–18:00 weekdays and to 18:30 weekends.
quote: Summer opening hours (March 29, 2026 – November 1, 2026) Monday to Friday from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Saturday and Sunday from 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.

claim: The CGN N1 ferry from Lausanne-Ouchy to Évian-les-Bains crosses Lake Geneva in about 35 minutes for CHF 22 second class / CHF 31 first, but from 2026 CGN has roughly halved crossings, concentrating them around commuter hours.
quote: From 2026, the number of ferries crossing Lake Geneva is reduced, with passenger ferry boats mostly operating during commuting hours.

claim: CGN publishes the official 2026 timetable and ticketing for Lake Geneva passenger boats including the Lausanne-Ouchy–Évian-les-Bains N1 line.
quote: CGN | Timetables & Tickets

claim: Café Romand on Place Saint-François is a Belle Epoque brasserie open since 1951, awarded 'Café historique de Lausanne' in 2021, serving papet vaudois, moitié-moitié fondue, and malakoffs.
quote: Café Romand sits on Place Saint-François 2 in downtown Lausanne... It's a historic brasserie with 'Belle Epoque' decor that has retained its original character since 1951... Signature dishes include 'papet vaudois', half-and-half fondue, and malakoffs.

claim: La Pinte Besson, founded in 1780, is the oldest café in Lausanne and has a vaulted cellar-bar atmosphere with a fondue with morels and cognac.
quote: Founded in 1780, Pinte Besson is the oldest café in Lausanne. The ground floor offers a fondue with morels and cognac in a cellar bar atmosphere from 1870.

claim: Time Out confirms Pinte Besson 'claims to be the oldest pub in Lausanne, and was set up by a wine merchant in 1780' and notes Brasserie de Montbenon occupies a prime spot in Montbenon park.
quote: Claims to be the oldest pub in Lausanne, and was set up by a wine merchant in 1780... Opened at the end of 2014, this stylish brasserie occupies a prime location on the classy (and grassy) Montbenon park

claim: Café du Grütli at Rue de la Mercerie 4 is a family-run Swiss restaurant specializing in fondue, seasonal Vaudois dishes, and 'La Chasse des Grisons' game menu, run by the Prutsch family.
quote: Rue de la Mercerie 4, CH-1003 Lausanne... The café specializes in traditional Swiss cuisine. They feature fondue as a signature offering, with menus highlighting 'produits frais de saison'.

claim: Café du Vieil Ouchy at Place du Port 3 is a lakeside historic café (labelled 'Café historique de Lausanne' in 2021) serving cheese fondue, Lake Geneva perch fillets, and meringues with double cream.
quote: Cheese fondue is the restaurant's signature offering. The menu also features regional dishes including cordon bleu and Lake Geneva perch fillets. The establishment is known for its desserts, particularly 'meringues with double cream'.

claim: Café de Grancy on Boulevard de Grancy below the station is a bistro doing weekend brunch (10:00–15:00 Sat/Sun), Wednesday fondue nights, and seasonal contemporary cooking with a library and terrace.
quote: Brunchs are organized every Saturday and Sunday, with service available from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM... Wednesday evenings feature fondue nights with original options... The cuisine oscillates between bistro and gastronomy, prioritizing seasons and local products.

claim: Ta Cave at Rue du Simplon 35 is Switzerland's first crowdfunded wine bar (opened 2015) with a monthly-rotating list of six to ten picks plus discovery wines, snack boards, and a Meule cheese-mould bread.
quote: Ta Cave is Switzerland's first crowdfunded wine bar... a selection of six to ten best wine picks every month and eight discovery wines... A notable specialty is 'the delicious La Meule bread, baked in cheese moulds'.

claim: Lausanne's curated wine-bar shortlist also includes Le 20 (Petit-Chêne 11), Vintage (Langallerie 7), Vinothèque du Château d'Ouchy (Place du Port), and Street Cellar in the Flon (Port-Franc 2a).
quote: Le 20 (Rue du Petit-Chêne 11)... Vintage wine bar (Rue Langallerie 7)... Vinothèque du Château d'Ouchy (Place du Port)... Ta Cave (Rue du Simplon 35)... Street Cellar (Rue du Port-Franc 2a)

claim: The Flon district concentrates bars and restaurants including King Size Pub, Les Jardins de PAM rooftop, Barberousse rum bar, Cipriano Wine & Ham, Brasserie Belleville, Forbici (Italian), and TAO lounge.
quote: Street Cellar (Wine bar) / King Size Pub (Pub with giant screen) / Les Jardins de PAM (Rooftop bar) / Barberousse (Rum bar) / Cipriano Wine & Ham (Café bar) / Brasserie Belleville / Forbici / TAO (Lounge bar-restaurant)

claim: Top Tripadvisor picks near the Cathédrale include Amici (Italian, 4.4), Brasserie Les 100 Suisses (Swiss, 4.9), Creperie la Chandeleur with a cathedral view, and Vieux-Lausanne Restaurant & Giraf Bar in the old town.
quote: Amici (4.4★) - Italian Mediterranean... Brasserie Les 100 Suisses (4.9★) - Swiss European cuisine featuring 'Very friendly service'... Creperie la Chandeleur (4.2★) - French European creperie with 'great view'... Vieux-Lausanne Restaurant & Giraf Bar (4.4★) - French and Swiss dining in a 'Historical place in old town'

claim: Lausanne Tourisme's brunch/bakery picks include Bread Store (run by 'Best Worker in France' baker Thomas Marie), Bryo 'The Brioche House', gluten/lactose-free El Gato Pâtisserie, Maison Buet, and Bel-Air Coffee.
quote: Awarded the title of Best Worker in France, baker Thomas Marie offers... Bryo, known as The Brioche House, is a new spot in Lausanne focused on... El Gato... first gluten- and lactose-free patisserie in Lausanne... Maison Buet... This artisan bakery and chocolate shop runs a café boutique

claim: The Lausanne Guide's specialty-coffee shortlist highlights Bel-Air Coffee (Scandi feel), Ça Passe Crème, Sleepy Bear (run by Diana), Bold Coffee Club in Sous-Gare, Ordinary Man on Petit-Chêne (roasted on-site), and The Coffee Project.
quote: Bel-Air Coffee: This stylish coffee shop has a Scandi feel to it... Sleepy Bear: Diana and her team's knowledge and passion about coffee permeate each cup... Bold Coffee Club: Located in sous gare... Ordinary Man Coffee: A café slash art gallery located right on Petit Chene

claim: The Lausanne Transport Card is given by accommodation on arrival, valid for the whole stay (up to 15 days), and includes free bus/train/metro in Lausanne, Lavaux and Parc naturel du Jorat plus the first journey to the accommodation.
quote: This personal card is given to every visitor by their accommodation when they arrive at their place of stay. It is valid for the period of the visitor's reservation including the day of arrival and day of departure (up to a maximum of 15 days).

claim: The Lausanne Transport Card gives free 2nd-class travel in zones 11, 12, 15, 16, 18 and 19 of the Mobilis network for guests paying the tourist tax.
quote: This personal card gives free travel on Lausanne's public transport system for each guest staying in a hotel and paying the tourist tax for overnight stays... in the following zones 11, 12, 15, 16, 18 and 19 (2nd class).

claim: The Geneva Airport to Lausanne train runs about 77 times a day on SBB, averaging 53 minutes with the fastest service in 49 minutes; first train 00:19, last 23:28.
quote: around 53 minutes... around 77 trains per day... First train departs at 00:19; last train at 23:28... SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) is identified as the main operator of services on this route.

claim: Train tickets from Geneva Airport to Lausanne on SBB start from around €9 (~CHF 9-11).
quote: GENEVA INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT to LAUSANNE train from $11 (€9) with SBB

claim: Lausanne's metro has two lines: the 7.8 km M1 (Flon to Renens, opened 1991) and the 5.9 km M2 (Ouchy-Olympique to Croisettes/Epalinges, opened 2008), the latter a fully automated rubber-tyred driverless metro.
quote: Line M1... 7.8 kilometres (4.8 mi)... Lausanne-Flon... to Renens... Line M2... 5.9 kilometres (3.7 mi)... fully automated, rubber-tyred metro... opened 27 October 2008.

claim: The M2 is the world's steepest metro, with an average gradient of 5.7% and slopes up to 12%, climbing roughly 338 m of elevation between Ouchy on the lake and Croisettes uphill.
quote: the world's steepest metro... an average incline of 5.7%, and as steep as 12% in some places... rubber-tyred metro was selected to counter these, the steepest slopes of any similar adhesion-worked system in the world.

claim: M1 and M2 metro lines run frequently, typically every 5-10 minutes (M2 every 3-5 minutes at peak), making transit the practical way to cover Lausanne's altitude changes.
quote: Both metro lines run frequently, typically every 5-10 minutes... For more specific M2 frequency data, frequency is typically every 3 to 5 minutes, and every 3 to 6 minutes on Sunday.

claim: Lausanne is not an easy walking city because of its three-hill terrain and steep gradients (especially the Old Town); the practical strategy is to combine walking with the M2 metro and funiculars to handle the inclines.
quote: Lausanne is generally not considered an 'easy' city to walk around due to its famously hilly terrain and steep gradients, especially in the Old Town... combine walking with public transport, using the metro or a bus to conquer the steepest inclines.

claim: Lausanne in May averages around 17°C daytime and 9°C at night, with ~126 mm of rainfall and ~212 hours of sunshine.
quote: Lausanne May temperature around 17°C (63°F), with daytime temperatures usually reaching up to 17°C and nighttime temperatures falling to approximately 9°C... averaging around 126 mm for the month... about 212 hours of sunshine.

claim: Lausanne in June averages 21°C daytime and 13°C at night with around 120 mm of rain and 238 sunshine hours — pack layers, a light jacket for evenings, and waterproof gear.
quote: Lausanne June temperature around 21°C (70°F)... cooling down at night to around 13°C... averaging around 120 mm for the month... around 238 hours of sunshine.

claim: Best base areas: Flon/centre for nightlife, dining and metro access; Ouchy for a relaxed lakeside promenade feel; Vieille-Ville/La Cité for medieval streets around the cathedral but with a daily uphill workout.
quote: Flon is a dynamic neighbourhood blending historical charm and modern flair, with vibrant nightlife... Ouchy sits directly on the waterfront and has a much more relaxed feel... La Cité district, where the Cathedral of Notre Dame... if you choose to stay in this area, be prepared for a daily workout as you climb the hill!

claim: Two to three days (a weekend) is the recommended length of stay for Lausanne — enough for museums, Old Town, lakeside and dining without feeling rushed.
quote: With a weekend (two to three days) in Lausanne, you'll have a bit more time to enjoy everything that the city has to offer... Three days is more than enough time to see pretty much everything in Lausanne.
